answer_summary: Q = aluminium (Al, Z = 13, Ar = 26.98); C·xH2O = AlF3·3H2O (x = 3); D = Na3AlF6 (cryolite). All three printed percentages reproduce inside their displayed half-quantum windows: w(H2O) = 54.048/138.028 = 39.1577…% (printed 39.16%), w(Na) = 68.97/209.94 = 32.8523…% (printed 32.85%), w(Q) = 26.98/209.94 = 12.8513…% (printed 12.85%). Uniqueness proved: the v = 2 family forces 17.9725 < Ar < 17.997, contradicted by the periodic table (O 16.00, F 19.00); the v = 3 family forces 26.945 < Ar < 26.9943, matching exactly one printed element, aluminium 26.98; at the tightened aluminium mass the hydration and sodium data force x = 3 and n = 3.
assumptions: M-A4-1: C = QF_v with v in {2,3} (common metal-fluoride stoichiometries), hydrate QF_v·xH2O, x ≥ 1
M-A4-2: D = C adduct n NaF = Na_n Q F_{v+n}, n ≥ 1 (as cryolite Na3AlF6 = AlF3 ⬝ 3 NaF)
M-A4-4: after identification the true Ar(Q) lies within half a displayed quantum (±0.005) of the matched printed periodic-table value (printed masses are measurements at half-quantum precision)
source_gaps: The problem text does not print the valence restriction v ∈ {2,3}; it is chemically standard. Widening to v ≤ 5 admits one spurious numerically self-similar candidate (v,x,n) = (5,5,5) near scandium's printed Ar 44.96, but ScF5 does not exist (Sc is exclusively +3), so the chemical answer is unchanged; the restriction is declared as assumption M-A4-1 rather than derived.

The exact structural class D = Na_n Q F_{v+n} (fluoride adduct of C with NaF) is a standard chemical reading of 'C reacts with excess NaF to yield D' containing both Na and Q; it is declared as M-A4-2.
Interpreting the printed periodic-table masses as half-quantum measurements (M-A4-4) follows the task measurement policy but is not spelled out in the problem text itself.
